analysis.title: Latham Group Inc. (SWIM): 3Q26 Recap: Efforts to Gain Share in the Sand States Support Market Relative Outperformance as We Look to 2027
key_insights: GS keeps its Sell rating on SWIM and raises the 12-month price target to $6.00 from $5.50 against a $7.32 price, implying 18.0% downside. The target rests on 7.5x (was 6.5x) new Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA, with the higher multiple reflecting confidence in the secular shift to fiberglass pools.

3Q26 adj. EBITDA was $45.3mn, below the GS estimate of $46.3mn and roughly in line with FactSet consensus of $45.1mn. The adj. EBITDA margin of 24.8% was 26bps below the GS model, and gross margin was 87bps below the model, with higher sales and marketing expense also weighing.

3Q sales grew 12.5% against a GS estimate of +14%. In-ground pools rose 23% (14% organic), covers rose 9%, and liners fell 5%, which management tied to macro pressure on a value-oriented segment and a tough comparison.

Share gains in the Sand States are the main support for the story. National leads are up 25% YTD (Florida +89%, Texas +115%), and a targeted initiative across three Florida neighborhoods produced 15 incremental pool purchases.

Commercial build-out is progressing. The Florida team is nearly fully staffed, Texas hiring should finish by year-end, Arizona entry is planned for January, and a new Chief Commercial Officer will focus on the builder channel. A national homebuilder will offer Latham fiberglass pools in Florida, focused on the move-up and custom-built segments.

Management estimates fiberglass is at least 25% of the U.S. in-ground pool market, up 1pt YOY, with a path to 35%-40% over time. GS believes Latham is positioned to outperform management's expectation of a flat pool market in 2027.

3Q gross margin expanded 130bps YOY to 36.7% on better absorption, resolution of 2Q operating constraints, and lean manufacturing and value engineering. SG&A rose $7mn, and adj. EBITDA margin rose about 110bps YOY to 24.8%.

Pricing added about 200bps to organic growth in 3Q. Higher transportation costs and commodity inflation, including elevated oil prices, were headwinds. Latham raised its fuel surcharge and priced liners and autocovers, which GS expects to help price/cost from 4Q.

GS cuts its 2026 revenue estimate to $611mn (7.4% organic, 11.9% including M&A), near the midpoint of guidance. 2026 EBITDA goes to $115.5mn from $117.6mn (18.9% margin, up 61bps YOY) against the guide of $112-118mn.

Out-year estimates are cut harder. 2027 EBITDA goes to $126.2mn from $139.5mn and 2028 to $136.5mn from $152.0mn. 2027 EPS falls to $0.23 from $0.33 and 2028 EPS to $0.29 from $0.41, with 2027 revenue growth modeled at 4.5% on greater macro headwinds.

Balance sheet: net debt/adj. EBITDA was 1.8x, down from 2.2x in 2Q26 and 2.3x a year ago, with $94.8mn of cash and $43mn of FCF. GS expects year-end leverage of 1.7x against the guide of under 2.0x, and 2026 capex guidance holds at about $43mn.
The Board authorized a new three-year, $100mn share buyback program. Management also reiterated interest in medium-sized, accretive M&A.

GS sees unfavorable risk/reward at the current valuation. The upside case is $8.50 (30.0x 2027 EPS) and the downside case is $4.50 (22.0x 2027 EPS). It expects the economic backdrop and limited housing turnover to weigh on pool demand and drive peer-relative underperformance of the stock.

market_movers.rationale: Sell maintained and target raised to $6.00 from $5.50 on a 7.5x multiple (was 6.5x) of Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA. GS sees 18.0% downside from $7.32 and unfavorable risk/reward despite share gains in the Sand States.

earnings_insights: SWIM 3Q26 adj. EBITDA, reported 11/3-11/4 (adjusted basis): $45.3mn vs GS estimate $46.3mn and FactSet consensus $45.1mn. Adj. EBITDA margin 24.8% (reported), 26bps below the GS model.
SWIM 3Q26 sales, reported: +12.5% YOY vs GS estimate of +14%. In-ground pools +23% (+14% organic), covers +9%, liners -5%.
SWIM 3Q26 gross margin, reported: 36.7%, up 130bps YOY and 87bps below the GS model. SG&A up $7mn YOY.
SWIM guidance cited in the report: 2026 adj. EBITDA $112-118mn, capex about $43mn at the midpoint, year-end leverage under 2.0x. Management called for a flat pool market in 2027.

GS estimates (not reported): 2026E revenue $611.1mn (was $612.3mn), 2027E $638.5mn (was $657.5mn), 2028E $664.0mn. Comparable adj. EBITDA 2026E $115.5mn (was $117.6mn), 2027E $126.2mn (was $139.5mn), 2028E $136.5mn (was $152.0mn).

GS EPS estimates from the cover table (not reported): 2026E $0.24 (was $0.22), 2027E $0.23 (was $0.33), 2028E $0.29 (was $0.41). Quarterly estimates: 4Q26E $(0.05) and 1Q27E $(0.05), against a 3Q26 figure of $0.18 shown on the cover.
risk_factors: Rising macro uncertainty and limited housing turnover weighing on pool demand, with affordability and financing conditions shutting some consumers out of the market.
Weakness in liners, a value-oriented segment under macro pressure, facing a tough comparison.
Higher sales and marketing spend to scale the sales force, plus transportation costs and commodity inflation including elevated oil prices.
Valuation: GS sees unfavorable risk/reward, with a downside case of $4.50 (22.0x 2027 EPS) against an upside case of $8.50 (30.0x).
Upside risks to the Sell call: a larger shift to fiberglass pools, successful new products and distribution expansion, penetration of newer markets, and lower raw material costs improving price/cost.
geopolitical: Canadian tariffs and counter-tariffs are expected to have an immaterial impact on SWIM's 2026 results given proactive positioning of seasonal inventory.

tension_points.theme: SWIM fiberglass share gains vs valuation
tension_points.bull_case: Latham is gaining share in the Sand States, with national leads up 25% YTD, a national homebuilder partnership in Florida, and fiberglass at 25%+ of in-ground pools with a path to 35%-40%. GS believes this can beat management's flat 2027 pool market view and drive operating leverage.
tension_points.bear_case: GS expects the economic backdrop and limited housing turnover to weigh on pool demand. It sees the stock at 31.1x 2026E P/E with unfavorable risk/reward, a $6.00 target below the $7.32 price, and peer-relative underperformance.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The report ties the upside case ($8.50, 30.0x 2027 EPS) to a larger-than-expected shift to fiberglass pools or lower raw material costs improving price/cost, which would undercut the Sell call.

theme_stances.key_argument: Latham is well positioned to outperform management's expectation of a flat 2027 pool market by expanding into Texas and Arizona and gaining penetration in the builder channel.
The economic backdrop and limited housing turnover should weigh on pool demand and drive peer-relative underperformance in the stock.
theme_stances.evidence: limited housing turnover to weigh on demand for pools
